title: 2026-10-30_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_6a8
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activity, contain the threat, and ensure the system is secure.
outcomes: Determine network ports used for suspicious communication.
Analyze logs and network traffic for evidence of data exfiltration.
Collect forensic evidence supporting the identified malicious activity.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activity, contain the threat, and ensure the system is secure.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target host that communicates with an external server. The flag is the name of the suspicious service.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, run the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for the service named `systemkernelservicedefender.service`. This command lists all running services, and the suspicious service stands out due to its unusual name and description.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Check the running services and look for any that seem out of place or have unusual descriptions.

hints.title: Intermediate Hint
hints.content: Use the `systemctl` command to list all running services. The suspicious service will have an unusual name.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service is named `systemkernelservicedefender.service`. Use `systemctl list-units --type=service` to find it.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication identified in the previous task. The flag is the port number.
levels.solution: To determine the port used for the suspicious communication, inspect the service configuration file located at `/etc/systemd/system/systemkernelservicedefender.service` and look for the `ExecStart` line, which specifies the port number as an argument. The port number is the flag you need to find.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Examine the service configuration for the suspicious service to find the port number.

hints.title: Intermediate Hint
hints.content: Use the `cat` command to view the contents of the service configuration file at `/etc/systemd/system/systemkernelservicedefender.service`. Look for the `ExecStart` line.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The port number is specified as an argument in the `ExecStart` line of the service configuration file. It is `80`.

levels.title: Evidence Collection
levels.content: Collect forensic evidence supporting the identified malicious activity, including logs, process information, service configuration, and network evidence. The flag is the path to the script used for evidence collection.
levels.solution: To collect forensic evidence, run the script `/usr/local/bin/local-inventory.sh` which will gather relevant logs, process information, service configuration, and network evidence. The path to the script is the flag you need to find.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Look for logs and configuration files related to the suspicious service and any network connections it makes.

hints.title: Intermediate Hint
hints.content: The script for evidence collection is located in the `/usr/local/bin/` directory. Use the `ls` command to list the contents of this directory.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The script for evidence collection is named `local-inventory.sh` and is located at `/usr/local/bin/local-inventory.sh`.
